projects.title: A complete project plan for a real initiative
projects.summary: Take a real initiative of an association, a small business or your school (an event, a move, a new website) and build its full project plan: charter, work breakdown, Gantt chart with the critical path, budget, risk register, RACI and communication plan.
projects.why: Recruiters for junior project manager roles want to see that you can structure a project from a vague request. A complete, coherent plan for a real initiative is concrete proof, and it gives you a project to talk about in every interview.

data.name: Project management guides (Atlassian)
data.note: Short guides on charters, planning, risks and status reports.

data.name: Excel video training (Microsoft)

steps.title: Frame it
steps.text: Meet the person who needs the project (the sponsor). Write a one-page charter: goal, benefits, scope in and out, deadline, budget, constraints, success criteria.

steps.title: Stakeholders
steps.text: List everyone affected, with their interest and influence, and how you will involve each one.

steps.title: Break down the work
steps.text: Build a work breakdown structure: deliverables, then tasks small enough to estimate (1 to 5 days).

steps.title: Plan
steps.text: Put the tasks in Excel with durations and dependencies, draw the Gantt chart with conditional formatting, and mark the critical path and the milestones.

steps.title: Budget
steps.text: Cost each task (time, purchases, services) and add a contingency reserve for the main risks.

steps.title: Risks and roles
steps.text: Write a risk register (probability, impact, owner, response) and a RACI matrix for the main deliverables.

steps.title: Communication
steps.text: Plan the meetings and reports: who gets what, how often, in which format. Write the first status report.

deliverables: The Excel plan with the Gantt chart, milestones and critical path
The risk register and the RACI matrix
The communication plan and a first status report
checklist: The scope says clearly what is out of the project
Every task has an owner, a duration and its dependencies
The critical path is marked and goes from the start to the end
The budget adds up and includes a contingency reserve
Each high risk has a response and an owner
Each deliverable has exactly one Accountable in the RACI

cv.bullet: Planned [initiative] end to end (personal project): project charter, work breakdown, Gantt chart with critical path, budget with contingency, risk register, RACI and communication plan.
cv.talk: Walk through your critical path, the biggest risk you found and how your plan would change if the deadline moved two weeks earlier.

stretch: Rebuild the plan in a project tool (MS Project trial, Smartsheet or Jira) and compare.
Run a short risk workshop with the real sponsor.
Write the lessons learned as if the project had ended.

projects.title: A project portfolio status dashboard in Power BI
projects.summary: Download real project data from the World Bank (budgets, dates, status) and build a one-page portfolio dashboard in Power BI for a steering committee: progress, budget, delays and the projects that need a decision.
projects.why: Project managers and PMO analysts report to steering committees every month. A clear portfolio dashboard on real data shows you know what decision-makers need to see, and Power BI appears in many PMO offers.

data.name: World Bank projects and operations
data.note: Thousands of real projects with commitment amounts, approval and closing dates, status and sector, downloadable.

data.name: Power BI financial sample (Microsoft Learn)
data.note: How to get Power BI Desktop and a sample to practise with before your own data.

data.name: Project management guides (Atlassian)
data.note: What goes into a status report and a steering committee.

steps.title: Get the data
steps.text: On the World Bank projects site, filter one region or sector and download the list of projects as Excel or CSV.

steps.title: Clean it
steps.text: Load it in Power BI, set the types, and create columns: duration planned, months since approval, status group.

steps.title: Define the indicators
steps.text: Choose 4 to 6 indicators a steering committee needs: number of active projects, total commitment, projects past their planned closing date, share by status.

steps.title: Build the page
steps.text: One page: the indicators at the top, a timeline of projects, a breakdown by sector and a table of projects that need attention.

steps.title: Add the narrative
steps.text: Write three comments a project director would say: what is going well, what is late, what decision is needed.

steps.title: Check it
steps.text: Show it to someone who does not know the data: can they say in one minute which projects need a decision?

deliverables: The Power BI file (or screenshots) with the one-page dashboard
The list of indicators and how each one is calculated
Three written comments for the steering committee
A short README linked from your CV
checklist: Every indicator has a written definition
Dates are real dates, not text, and late projects are computed, not typed
The page reads from top (summary) to bottom (detail)
Colours mean the same thing everywhere (late is always the same colour)
The table shows only the projects that need a decision
The comments say what to decide, not only what the chart shows

cv.bullet: Built a project portfolio dashboard in Power BI on [n] real World Bank projects (personal project): status, commitments, delays and a steering committee summary.
cv.talk: Explain how you decided a project was late, and what the steering committee should decide from your dashboard.

stretch: Add a drill-through page with the details of one project.
Schedule a refresh from the downloaded file and document it.
Rebuild the same page in Excel and compare which is easier to maintain.

projects.title: Run a hybrid project: milestone plan and Kanban delivery
projects.summary: Run a small real project for four weeks (a website for an association, an event, a study group) with a milestone plan for the sponsor and a Kanban board for the work, and report weekly with a status update, a RAID log and a final retrospective.
projects.why: Most companies run hybrid projects: fixed milestones for management, agile teams doing the work. Showing you have run both at once, with honest reporting and change handled properly, matches what IT project manager offers ask for.

data.name: The Kanban Guide
data.note: The official short guide: visualise the work, limit work in progress, measure flow.

data.name: Project management guides (Atlassian)
data.note: Status reports, risks and change requests.

steps.title: Agree the milestones
steps.text: With the sponsor, set 3 or 4 milestones over four weeks and what done means for each.

steps.title: Set up the board
steps.text: Create a Kanban board with work-in-progress limits, and the backlog of tasks for the first milestone.

steps.title: Run the weekly rhythm
steps.text: Each week: update the board, the RAID log (risks, assumptions, issues, dependencies) and send a one-page status with a green, amber or red rating.

steps.title: Handle a change
steps.text: When the sponsor asks for something new, write a change request with its impact on time and scope, and record the decision.

steps.title: Measure the flow
steps.text: Track cycle time and throughput each week, and use them to forecast whether the next milestone is safe.

steps.title: Close
steps.text: Hand over the result, run a retrospective with the people involved, and write the lessons learned.

deliverables: The milestone plan and the Kanban board (screenshots)
The RAID log and at least one change request with its decision
checklist: Each milestone has a written definition of done
WIP limits are set and respected (or the exceptions are explained)
Each status rating has a reason, and an amber or red comes with an action
The change request shows the impact before the decision
The forecast uses measured throughput, not hope
Lessons learned say what you would do differently

cv.bullet: Ran a 4-week hybrid project for [organisation] (volunteer project): milestone plan, Kanban delivery with WIP limits, weekly status reports, RAID log and change control.
cv.talk: Tell how you handled the change request: what it cost, who decided, and how you told the team and the sponsor.

stretch: Compare your forecast from throughput with what really happened at each milestone.
Add a simple budget and track it in the weekly status.
Turn the lessons learned into a one-page checklist for the next project.
